Read XBRL filings

Source: R/read_xbrl.R
read_xbrl.Rd

Reads one filing, a vector of them, or a whole directory, and returns a single tibble with one row per reported fact. The taxonomy is resolved as the filings are read, so labels, the statement hierarchy and the debit/credit marking arrive with the facts rather than in a second step.

Usage

read_xbrl(path, taxonomy = TRUE, recurse = TRUE, encoding = "UTF-8")

Arguments

path

A directory, a path to a single filing, or a vector of either. Directories contribute every .xml file they hold.

taxonomy

Resolve the taxonomy while reading. TRUE, the default, uses the tables packaged with cvrr – see cvrr_taxonomy_tables. Pass a cvrr_taxonomy from read_taxonomy() for a version those do not cover, or FALSE for the facts alone; add_taxonomy() does the same job afterwards.

recurse

Descend into subdirectories. Default TRUE, because filings are usually filed by year.

encoding

Character encoding of the files. Defaults to "UTF-8".

Value

A tibble with one row per fact: file, cvr, period_start, period_end, prev_start, prev_end, elementid (local name), prefix and namespace, contextid, fact (the text as tagged) and value (the same figure as a number, NA where the fact is text), unitid, unit, decimals, schemaref, startdate, enddate, instant, dimensions and explicit_member. With taxonomy, the columns add_taxonomy() adds. Dates are Date.

What an instance does and does not contain

An XBRL instance holds facts, contexts and units – and no human-readable text at all. That is by design: the meaning of every element lives in the taxonomy the filing points to with a single link:schemaRef. Labels, the statement hierarchy and the debit/credit balance are published there, and add_taxonomy() is what joins them on. XBRL also has a place for calculation weights, and the Danish taxonomy leaves it empty for the ordinary statements – see find_signs().

Because the taxonomy is keyed by qualified name, the element's namespace is returned alongside its local name. A Danish filing binds six or more namespaces at once (fsa for the financial statements, gsd for company data, mrv for management's review, arr for the auditor's report, ...), and elementid alone cannot be looked up.

Many filings, one table

Every row carries the filing it came from: file, cvr and the four dates of period_start, period_end, prev_start and prev_end. That is what makes a directory of filings usable as one table, and it is why nothing downstream takes a period argument any more – the period is a column.

Binding filings needs fill: each contributes only the dimension columns it actually uses, so a filing tagging classes of equity has a dim_ClassesOfEquity column and one that does not, does not. do.call(rbind, ...) fails on that, which is reason enough for this function to do the binding itself.

A filing that cannot be parsed does not stop the read. Its path is collected and all of them are reported once at the end, in attr(x, "failed").

Amounts are absolute

A monetary fact is stated in its unit – kroner, not thousands. The decimals attribute says how precise the figure is, not what scale it is on: decimals = "-3" means accurate to the nearest thousand, and the value is still in kroner. The "tkr." at the head of a printed note is a presentation choice for the human-readable text and does not reach the tags.

Confirmed against a filing whose note prints its fixed assets as 62.113 with the column headed tkr.: the tagged figure is 62113000.

A filing scaled wrong throughout is harder to catch than that, because it stays internally consistent: its balance sheet still balances and its income statement still reconciles. Registered capital looks like a check – an A/S must hold 400,000 kr, an ApS 40,000 – but it only works for the A/S. Danish entrepreneur companies (IVS) could be founded on a single krone until the form was abolished in 2021, and 75 filings in a corpus of 4,304 report capital under 1,000 kr with entirely ordinary assets. They are not scaled; they are IVS, and the filing does not state its own legal form.

What does catch it is a ratio between two reported figures that has to fall in a known range. Payroll divided by the employee count is the readiest one: a year of work costs somewhere between 100,000 and 1,500,000 kr, and a filing claiming 194 kr has scaled one of the two.

Dimensions

A context may carry several explicitMember elements, and in Danish filings roughly a fifth of them do. One of the common pairs is ConsolidatedSoloDimension, which says whether a figure is the group's or the parent's alone – so keeping only the first member would silently mix consolidated and solo amounts. All members are returned in explicit_member, semicolon-separated, with the dimension each belongs to in dimensions in the same order.

See also

xbrl_accounts() for the tables this feeds, add_taxonomy() to resolve the taxonomy separately, cvr_download() for fetching the filings.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# a whole directory, taxonomy and all
x <- read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl")

# one filing, facts only
read_xbrl("13645183_2024-12-31.xml", taxonomy = FALSE)
} # }
